The clock a slide draws moves 31 cells at maxD 6, an order of magnitude under the rasteriser's own noise. The Linux baseline is recorded and CI runs the gate, which caught two breaks a Windows-only run never could: the workflow had ordered Build after Lint, so `check` had been red on every push to main, a committed README linked to a gitignored file, and three of 3.7 font tests asserted what this machine has rather than what the code does | 3.10       | First npm release: `render-svg` and `cli render`                       | ⚠️ done        | [0045](../adr/phase-3-text/0045-the-face-box-belongs-to-the-rasteriser.md) — the plan called this a release and it was really a measurement: `render-svg` was already a pure string function that ran in Node, but text needed a canvas and there is none, so `pptx-studio render` reads the font own tables instead. That is a second measurement engine, and no real font can say what the first one does - Arial `hhea.ascender` and its `OS/2.usWinAscent` are both 1854 - so T13 built seven fonts that disagree with themselves on purpose and asked Chromium. The face box is `usWin`, or `sTypo` where `fsSelection` bit 7 is set (14/14, against 10/14 for `hhea`, which is what everybody writes first); pair kerning is GPOS where the font has a `kern` feature and the legacy table otherwise (42/42, against 36/42 for preferring the legacy one, which is the cheaper parse and wrong on every font carrying both); a width is each advance truncated and each kern rounded at 1/65536 px (252/252, against 88/252 for exact floats). The advance is linear in size to within 1.04e-4 px, which is the finding the whole approach rests on: the browser does not hint it. The reader reproduces all 252 widths exactly and 19 of 19 mutants die. Running the release path found that changesets/action renamed its four inputs, so Release had been red on every push to main since 0.1, and that no package carried a LICENSE or a NOTICE, which Apache-2.0 4(a) and 4(d) require and ours is not decorative - it carries POI attribution for the 187 presets Finishing it found that nothing had ever installed the eleven packages - pkg:qa inspects a tarball shape and apps/studio resolves through the link farm - so examples/nextjs-studio installs them from the registry instead, and 194 of 194 XML parts re-emit byte-identical through real tarballs. Consuming the published API from outside showed renderDeck taking the verb options rather than the drawing ones, which is now RenderDeckOptions and a breaking 0.2.0. Two of 0042 five open questions close: the ideographic baseline is the BASE ideo coordinate of the DFLT script and not the descent, 30 of 30, so the shipped reading was wrong on any face carrying one, and Chromium reads DFLT alone, never the run script, with no fall-through when it is absent; and trunc against floor is foreclosed by hmtx.advanceWidth being a UFWORD rather than unmeasured, so the probe 0042 asked for cannot be built. T14 then ran on a Linux runner for the first time and went red on three defects in shipped code: the reader skipped type 9 Extension GPOS lookups, so eighteen Lato faces got no kerning at all and measured Latin about 8 percent wide, silently; renderDeck threw CLI_NO_FACE on a machine holding 53 usable faces, where the whole point of the font guard is to substitute and report; and the face box is 75.8 px out on the descent of three Japanese faces, which is still open. It also refuted 0042 own width finding: all 3420 browser widths on Linux are whole pixels, so the claim that the browser does not hint the advance was true of seven fonts carrying no hinting program and never generalised, and the gate premise had to be re-derived from per-glyph rounding rather than from exactness. The next run answered the face box it had left open, and the answer was that the question was malformed: there is no one table. DirectWrite reads usWin and FreeType reads hhea, bit 7 moving both onto sTypo, and neither reading fits both platforms - 12/12 against Windows and 76/79 against Linux for the first, 79/79 and 7/12 for the second, missing by 75.8 px and 100 px on a 1000 px em. So the shipped reader was not wrong, it was answering for one rasteriser while running on the other, and metricsOf now takes the backend its host resolves. The Extension fix held: 228 width failures fell to 6, all on Lato, and those turned out to be the tolerance rather than the reader - the browser rounds the advance and the kern adjustment separately, so a run carries one rounding per glyph and one per applied kern. A joint rounding is refuted rather than assumed, because it cannot cost the 0.648 px a glyph Lato Thin measures where every kern-free sample stays under 0.45, and only a 2000 unit em shows it at all, since it puts every value on a half pixel exactly where a 1000 em is exact and a 2048 one cancels. — all eleven packages are on npm at 0.1.0 with provenance. A trusted publisher cannot be attached to a package that does not exist, so the first publish went out from a one-time token job that has since been deleted. Releases are dispatched by hand from the Actions tab now: there is no version pull request, so the repository does not need "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests", which is a single toggle covering both verbs. No PNG - rasterising means shipping a rasteriser, and the point of the verb is that it needs nothing but Node. No shaping, so Arabic and Devanagari measure wide - T14 records the ratio rather than gating it, and that number, the reader agreement with Chromium on a real face and the face box on a 2048-em one all have their answers now. What is still open is macOS, which is neither rasteriser measured and takes the DirectWrite reading by assumption, and that a deck rendered on one platform and viewed on another has two answers to the same question. |

## Carried debt

Open across sub-phases, and not owned by any of them.

### `packages/validate` is still at 1.2's 29 rules

Four text sub-phases each identified rules that belong in the repair firewall and none were added: `p:kinsoku/@lang`, three `bodyPr` rules, `@panose` shape, and `@u`/`@strike` simple types.

Raised in: ADR 0029, ADR 0032, ADR 0033, ADR 0034.

### The registry canary pins ^0.1.0

examples/nextjs-studio installs @pptx-studio/* from npm at ^0.1.0, which is what makes it a canary. The day 0.2.0 publishes it keeps compiling against the previous API and goes quiet rather than red, so the bump is a deliberate act somebody has to make.

Raised in: ADR 0043.

### The twelfth package has no trusted publisher

render-dom sits at 0.0.0 in changesets ignore, so mountSlide and mountOverlay cannot be installed. Which workflow may publish over OIDC is a setting on each npm package and nothing in this tree asserts it, so its first release fails until someone adds it on npmjs.com by hand.

Raised in: ADR 0042, ADR 0043.

### A whole-pixel browser cannot separate the sub-pixel readings

Chromium on Linux reports every advance and every face box in whole pixels, so T13 four quantisation readings score within one row of each other and the four face-box variants separate not at all. T13 on Windows is the only experiment that can tell them apart, and nothing re-checks that they still agree.

Raised in: ADR 0044.

### Turbo reported FULL TURBO over changed sources

pnpm build cache-hit @pptx-studio/cli twice with edited sources in the tree and left a stale dist. Every ground-truth experiment scores packages/cli/dist, so a stale dist means scoring the previous reader; --force --no-daemon built correctly. Until this is understood, no experiment scoring dist is trustworthy without --force.

Raised in: ADR 0044.
